messages:
sre-oncall: :rotating_light: incident-bot paging: p99 tail latency spike detected on streaming route `/v1/stream/generate` for model `rw-7b-int8-calv4` in us-west-2. p95 ~ 420ms (ok), p99 ~ 3.2s (breach). streaming stalls observed (clients reporting stalled token delivery). alert: latency-slo:production:streaming p99 > 2s

incident-bot: [AUTO] AlertID=ALRT-1951112222 route=/v1/stream/generate model=rw-7b-int8-calv4 region=us-west-2 severity=high

prod-jess: seeing the same on dashboards — spike starts at 02:34 UTC. Rolling window shows correlations with the recent precision profile rollout `precision-profile/exp-int8-calib-v4` from 02:20 UTC.

ml-morgan: confirmed. We shipped that calibration yesterday to improve token throughput. Looks like KV cache lookups after calibration are causing degraded mem access pattern — long tail during dequant calls.

infra-kai: logs show repeated GC-ish pauses on the inference worker and some retries on the quant library. Sample worker trace: ```
[02:36:11] DEQ_CALL start seq=1
[02:36:11] KV_CACHE lookup miss id=0x7f34
[02:36:12] QUANT_DEQ fallback slow-path 1.2s
[02:36:13] STREAM_SEND token_index=12 delay=1.8s
```

eng-lead-mike: can we route traffic to a stable variant? We have `rw-7b-fp16-stable` and `rw-7b-int8-calv3` in catalog. Suggest immediate fallback to fp16 for streaming traffic and stop int8 rollout.

sre-oncall: agreed. Proposed live mitigations: 1) rollback precision-profile -> revert to `exp-int8-calib-v3` (older int8) OR 2) route streaming traffic to `rw-7b-fp16-stable` until further analysis. Which is faster?

ml-morgan: rollback of the profile requires a canary rollback across 3 deployment shards — will take ~6-8min to fully propagate and has risk of leftover cache mismatch. Routing is faster: can adjust routing policy to prefer fp16 for streaming in us-west-2 immediately.

infra-kai: I'll flip routing. Updating routing policy now: ```
# kube exec to routing service
kubectl patch configmap routing-policies -n rwd --type merge -p '{"data":{"streaming.preferred_models.us-west-2":"rw-7b-fp16-stable,rw-7b-int8-calv4"}}'
```

infra-kai: patched. Pushed split: streaming traffic -> 95% rw-7b-fp16-stable, 5% rw-7b-int8-calv4 (canary). Please monitor.

prod-jess: dashboards show p99 dropping back toward baseline within the next 90s. p99 ~ 560ms now. Customers reporting fewer stalls.

cs-olivia: CS: we have 7 open support threads claiming stalled streams/timeouts, some customers (enterprise tenants A & B) saw partial failures in live chat integrations. Impact estimate: ~1.8% of streaming sessions in us-west-2 between 02:30–02:40 UTC. Will notify affected customers with mitigation notes.

ml-morgan: starting deeper repro locally with the int8 calibration to reproduce KV dequant tail. Capturing perf traces and quant library counters.

infra-kai: also throttled continuous batching for the canary nodes to reduce tail amplification: ```
# disable continuous batching on shard canary
POST /admin/shards/us-west-2/canary/actions {"continuous_batching": false}
```

sre-oncall: note: reduced batching increases cost but reduces tail. Good short-term trade.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] Routing policy change applied by infra-kai at 02:37:12 UTC. Escalation state -> mitigated.

eng-lead-mike: start a postmortem runbook entry — mark root-cause candidate as "calibration fallout causing slow-path dequant calls under production KV patterns". Assign to ml-morgan and infra-kai for RCA.

prod-jess: oncall handoff incoming — I'm out in 18 minutes. Next oncall is eng-lead-mike. Mike, please take ownership of the incident until resolved.

eng-lead-mike: taking it. Checklist: 1) keep routing pref to fp16 for streaming 2) collect traces from 02:20–02:40 3) block further int8 profile rollouts 4) notify dedicated customers and CS for potential credits 5) schedule postmortem meeting.

cs-olivia: sending initial customer notification now: "We detected degraded streaming performance earlier; we have rolled user traffic to a stable variant and are working on a fix. We will follow up with root cause and remediation steps."

sre-oncall: running a quick SLO impact calc — based on traffic and breach window, estimated SLO impact: p99 breaches affected 1.4% of total monthly requests for the streaming SLO for the period. Draft note for ops: "SLO alert triggered, transient breach resolved by routing fallback; ongoing RCA."

ml-morgan: confirmed repro: under production-like KV distribution the int8 calibrated dequant path enters a fallback that is O(N) in some token patterns, causing 1–2s stalls intermittently. Fix vectors: update quant library to avoid fallback path OR relax calibration aggressiveness.

eng-lead-mike: next steps: 1) keep routing pref for 4 hours while we harden int8 calibration 2) schedule rollback of `exp-int8-calib-v4` in the model catalog to prevent accidental rollouts 3) prepare test harness improvement to inject KV-hit/miss patterns.

prod-jess: preparing the rollout block — creating temp lock in catalog: ```
PATCH /catalog/models/rw-7b-int8-calv4 {"lifecycle": "blocked", "block_reason": "calib-fallout-1951112222"}
```

infra-kai: lock applied. Also created a small dedicated pool with quant-disabled nodes for critical customers if needed.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] At 02:47:10 UTC mitigation confirmed, p99 stabilized across monitored regions. Incident state -> monitoring.

eng-lead-mike: handing over long-term owner for RCA to ml-morgan. I'll lead the postmortem and coordinate CS communications. Oncall log: `1951112222` — cause: calibration fallout, mitigation: routing fallback to fp16, follow-up: quant library fix and improved canary tests.

sre-oncall: handoff to eng-lead-mike acknowledged. I'm available for wakeup if we see re-escalation.

cs-olivia: CS log updated; outreach templates sent to affected customers.

ml-morgan: capturing all traces and starting a branch to add safety checks in the quant path. Will include perf counters and a toggle to short-circuit fallback.

prod-jess: thanks all. We'll reconvene for postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Adding owners to the calendar. :thumbsup:

eng-lead-mike: closing incident thread; leaving monitoring on for 2 hours. If anything pops, tag @eng-lead-mike and @sre-oncall.
